name: mercedes-logbook
description: Home Assistant integration that logs every trip of a Mercedes EV or plug-in hybrid (through mbapi2020), with a dashboard card: trip map, period filters and stats.
description_good_justification: The README's first paragraph: a Home Assistant integration that logs every trip of a Mercedes EV or plug-in hybrid (through mbapi2020), with a dashboard card. https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#readme
interact_justification: The README explains how to install it (HACS or manually), configure and use it. Feedback goes through GitHub issues and Discussions, contributions through pull requests (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
contribution_justification: Issues and pull requests on GitHub, as https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md explains.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: the CI must pass (ruff, pytest with a coverage floor, Hypothesis fuzzing, ESLint, npm audit, browser tests, HACS and hassfest validation, CodeQL), new functionality comes with tests, docs follow the change, style rules.
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers requirements, installation, configuration, the card, the sensors, the REST API, the database, troubleshooting and how it works: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#readme
documentation_interface_justification: The external interfaces are the config flow options, the sensors and the REST API, each documented in the README: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#configuration, https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#sensors, https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#rest-api
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
repo_interim_justification: Every change goes through a public pull request and lands on the public main branch between releases.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version vX.Y.Z, in manifest.json, the git tag and the GitHub release.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning: the release workflow bumps patch, minor or major.
version_tags_justification: The release workflow tags every release in git (vX.Y.Z): https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and the notes of each GitHub release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed so far. Fixes will be named in the release notes and in a GitHub security advisory (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed so far; the maintainer watches and answers the issue tracker (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/issues).
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed so far; ideas go to Discussions, which the maintainer watches (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/discussions).
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues and Discussions are public and searchable: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/issues?q=
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting through GitHub security advisories is enabled: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received so far; SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging within 7 days and assessing within 14.
build_justification: Nothing to build: the integration is Python and the card is a plain JavaScript module, both loaded as they are. The release workflow only packages the integration's folder into mercedes_trips.zip.
build_common_tools_justification: No build step; packaging is a short Python script (scripts/release.py package).
build_floss_tools_justification: No build step; the packaging, tests and linters (Python, pytest, ruff, Node.js, ESLint, Playwright) are all FLOSS.
test_justification: pytest tests in tests/ (with pytest-homeassistant-custom-component) and Playwright browser tests of the card in test/browser/, documented in the README: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#development
test_invocation_justification: pytest (integration) and npm test (card in a browser).
test_most_justification: CI enforces a coverage floor of 95 % (lines and branches, about 97 % today); the browser tests cover the card.
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: new functionality must come with tests, and a bug fix with a test that fails without it.
tests_are_added_justification: The tests, fuzzing and regression tests for the bugs they found were added in https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/pull/4; later changes add tests.
warnings_justification: ruff (pycodestyle, pyflakes, bugbear, bandit, pyupgrade and more) and ESLint's recommended rules run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any ruff finding or ESLint warning (--max-warnings 0), and the code has none.
warnings_strict_justification: ruff with a broad rule set including bandit's security rules, and ESLint with zero warnings tolerated, on the source, scripts and tests.
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer knows the principles of secure design and applies them here: least privilege (read-only workflow tokens, write access only in the jobs that publish; the integration changes nothing outside its own database), fail-safe defaults (unreadable states are ignored, invalid API parameters get a 400), complete mediation (every entity state and API parameter is validated), economy of mechanism (no runtime Python dependencies; Leaflet vendored, no CDN) and a small attack surface.
know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer knows the common errors behind vulnerabilities in this kind of software and how to counter them: XSS (addresses from Nominatim and every other text are escaped before they reach the page), SQL injection (parameterised queries only), information exposure (errors never echo exception text), resource exhaustion (bounded limit/offset), supply-chain attacks (pinned actions, locked dependencies, npm audit, Dependabot, an integrity check of the vendored Leaflet), leaked secrets (secret scanning and push protection), and crashes on malformed input (validation plus Hypothesis fuzzing).
crypto_published_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_call_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_floss_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_keylength_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_working_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_pfs_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The integration does not store passwords or any other credentials; Home Assistant handles authentication.
crypto_random_justification: The integration does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No security mechanism uses a weak algorithm. SHA-1 appears only as a cache-busting content hash for the card's URL, marked usedforsecurity=False.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases and the repository are only distributed over HTTPS from GitHub (HACS downloads from there).
delivery_unsigned_justification: Nothing is fetched over HTTP. HACS installs the release's mercedes_trips.zip over HTTPS, and each release carries its signed build-provenance attestation (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched vulnerabilities: CodeQL and npm audit run in CI, and Dependabot alerts are enabled.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: None known; Dependabot security updates are enabled.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Python, JavaScript and the workflows) with the security-extended queries on every pull request, on main and weekly: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml. ruff with bandit's rules too.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-extended queries and ruff's bandit rules look for common vulnerabilities (XSS, SQL injection, stack-trace exposure, unsafe workflows…).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No open CodeQL findings; the ones it raised (stack-trace exposure in the API's 400 messages, a file-system race in the dev server) were fixed in https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/pull/4.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit to a pull request and to main, and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based fuzzing with Hypothesis of the entity-state parsing, the API parameters and the database filters (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/tests/test_fuzz.py), and Playwright browser tests including an XSS test, on every pull request and before every release.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The tests run with assertions: pytest asserts, Hypothesis properties and Playwright expectations.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The fuzz tests found an OverflowError (an HTTP 500) when an hour or a trip id was too large for SQLite; fixed with regression tests in https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/pull/4.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the Python and browser tests on every pull request and on main: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
discussion_justification: GitHub issues, pull requests and Discussions: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/discussions
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials in the repository: GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled, and the release deploy key lives in Actions secrets.
english_justification: Documentation, code, issues and pull requests are in English (the UI is in English and Spanish).
hardening_justification: Parameterised SQL, validated and bounded API parameters, escaped output in the card, no eval or dynamic code, Leaflet and the font vendored (no CDN), errors that never echo exceptions, actions pinned to commits, read-only CI tokens and signed releases.
crypto_used_network_justification: Its only outgoing requests (Nominatim, and the card's OpenStreetMap tiles) use HTTPS.
crypto_tls12_justification: Requests go through Home Assistant's shared aiohttp session, whose SSL context (Python 3.14 defaults) only allows TLS 1.2 or later.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Home Assistant's aiohttp session verifies TLS certificates, and the integration never turns that off.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Coordinates go to Nominatim only over HTTPS with the certificate verified; no credentials are sent.
installation_common_justification: Installed, updated and removed through HACS, or by copying one folder into custom_components: the usual way for Home Assistant integrations.
dco_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#sign-off-dco: commits are signed off with the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 (git commit -s).
bus_factor_justification: One maintainer today. https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md describes how co-maintainers join and the continuity plan.
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/ROADMAP.md: plans until the end of 2027 and what is not planned.
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/SECURITY.md (what the integration reads, stores and sends, and who can read the trips) and https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md
documentation_current_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires the docs to follow every change; the README's images come from the demo with sample trips.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges next to the CI ones: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#readme
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The card follows the Home Assistant theme (light and dark), shows keyboard focus, uses real buttons with aria-expanded/aria-pressed and labelled groups, and respects reduced motion; the landing page does the same.
internationalization_justification: Texts are translated (translations/en.json and es.json for the integration, the card's string table for the card) and follow each user's language; dates, numbers and the 12/24-hour clock are formatted with Intl for the user's locale.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub and GitHub Pages) do not store passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Users update through HACS to the latest release; the changelog and release notes describe every change, versions follow SemVer, and breaking changes come with a major version and upgrade notes.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported in the last 12 months; SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters in the advisory.
coding_standards_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#style, ruff's configuration in pyproject.toml and ESLint's recommended rules (eslint.config.js).
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff check and npm run lint (--max-warnings 0) run in CI, so any finding fails the pull request.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries and no build step.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No build step: the shipped Python and JavaScript are the source itself, unminified.
build_non_recursive_justification: No build system; there are no recursive builds.
build_repeatable_justification: Reproducible: checking out a release tag and running python scripts/release.py package gives a byte-identical mercedes_trips.zip (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release).
installation_standard_variables_justific: Not installed into a POSIX file system: Home Assistant loads it from /config/custom_components.
installation_development_quick_justifica: pip install -r requirements_test.txt and pytest; npm ci and npm test or npm run demo: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook#development
external_dependencies_justification: manifest.json (no runtime requirements; the mbapi2020 integration provides the car's entities), requirements_test.txt for the tests, package.json and package-lock.json for the card's tools and Leaflet's version.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot alerts, security updates and monthly updates for pip, npm and the GitHub Actions; npm audit in CI.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Leaflet is pinned in package.json, where Dependabot updates it; node scripts/check-vendor.mjs --write refreshes the vendored copy and CI fails if the two differ.
interfaces_current_justification: Current Home Assistant APIs, tested against Home Assistant 2026.10; Dependabot keeps the test harness and tools up to date.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Python and browser tests run on every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Most of the bugs fixed before the test suite existed (October 2026) have no regression test; since then every fix comes with one, and the suite also covers several earlier fixes (the first odometer reading, the 500 while a trip is active, failed geocoding not being cached).
test_statement_coverage80_justification: About 97 % of lines and branches covered; CI enforces at least 95 %.
test_policy_mandated_justification: https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: new functionality must come with tests, and bug fixes with a regression test.
input_validation_justification: Entity states are parsed with range checks, the config flow's selectors bound every number, and the REST API validates every parameter (dates, hours, limit, offset, trip ids); see https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The integration implements no cryptography of its own. Its only network requests (Nominatim; the card's map tiles) are HTTPS through Home Assistant's aiohttp session and the browser.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are signed with Sigstore build-provenance attestations (.sigstore.json and .intoto.jsonl attached to each release); verify with gh attestation verify mercedes_trips.zip --repo dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook (https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release).
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags are annotated and created by the release workflow; the release files themselves are signed.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: regular releases and pull requests. https://github.com/dortizesquivel/mercedes-logbook/pulls?q=is%3Apr
